trajectory_summary: The call is a flat, procedural run through Verify that dead-ends at the credit qualifier. Energy never built because the rep didn't anchor the bill or interest reason before the hard gate, so when the DQ hit there was nothing to work with. The rep took the stated credit answer at face value and closed the pursuit in one breath.
outcome_dispute: This is arguably a DQ (credit_below_670) rather than a clean no_appointment, but per schema.qualifiers.credit_qualifier the setter DQ'd on stated credit with no attempt to question or verify — an unresolved policy question per spencer_operator_note about whether setters should DQ on stated score at all.

observed_outcome.quote: unfortunately, as of right now, it's not really gonna make sense for you guys, mainly because, you're not gonna see as much savings
observed_outcome.reasoning: Rep explicitly ends pursuit on the credit qualifier gate for both homeowner and co-owner, matching dq_rules.credit_below_670_no_alternative; no appointment was set or discussed.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The $120 bill was captured at 02:08 but the rep moved directly into the credit qualifier at 02:15 without ever tying the bill pain to the pitch or using it as leverage when the credit issue surfaced.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked the customer to send or read their utility bill during the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The customer's 'clean energy' interest reason from 00:29 was never referenced again, including at the point of disqualification where it could have been used to soften the exit or justify a genuine future follow-up.

objections.reasoning: This is a qualifier answer (credit score below threshold) rather than resistance to the script — a hard gate failing, not an objection to overcome, so it correctly triggers DQ rather than a rebuttal attempt.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Immediate concession on stated credit with no verification attempt
primary_coaching_focus.quote: unfortunately, as of right now, it's not really gonna make sense for you guys, mainly because, you're not gonna see as much savings
primary_coaching_focus.why: Per spencer_operator_note, stated credit and pulled credit can differ significantly; killing the lead on a self-reported number without asking whether it's an estimate or a known score risks losing a real deal — this is the single most consequential moment on the call.

key_moments.stewart_read: Rep captures the $120 bill but immediately moves to the credit qualifier without acknowledging or flipping it, losing the one emotional anchor available before the DQ.

key_moments.quote: all we ask of one of the homeowners is you guys just have a credit score of at least 670.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep runs the credit qualifier verbatim per the 670 threshold in the schema, correctly stated.

key_moments.quote: Yep. Well, it's a issue for me.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer states a disqualifying credit issue; per spencer_operator_note stated credit is unreliable, but rep neither questions it nor offers an alternative financing path before conceding the DQ.

key_moments.quote: I can notate here to just follow-up with you in a couple months
key_moments.stewart_read: The follow-up promise has no date, no time, and no owned next step — a soft exit dressed as a plan.
